tool: genfast2.js vs genfast.js (K0820 scripts/ verbatim baseline)
claim: byte-identical CNF for identical (w,m,q,options); genfast2.js replaces genfast.js's string-Map + double-gcd (v,rho) canonicalization by an exact integer key: (N480, RHO) = (480*v, 921600*rho^2) with N480 = -N*sc, sc = 480/(8*dy) in {60,30,20,15,12,10} for dy=1..6 (D = 8*(ya-yb) < 0), RHO = 230400*Ai + 4*(480*ya - N480)^2; the circle membership test becomes 230400*(2x-U)^2 + 4*(480y-N480)^2 === RHO (all exact integers). Same circle => same key without gcd, so the PAIRTHRESH=12 pair-witness census, exact scan, curve order/dedup and CNF encoding (reused verbatim from sat2.js via the S.buildCensus patch) are unchanged. Inner state: Int32Array/Float64Array open addressing (2^21 slots), per-U touched-slot list.

verification.method: generate CNF with both generators on 4 representative samples, byte-compare (cmp), record md5+size

notes: Coverage: q=8 with --rowY (rowsplit encoding), q=9, q=10 with --lex (H,V,HV), w=8 (q>=w+1 requirement exercised at w=8).

A first implementation dropped the negative sign of D = 8*(ya-yb) (N480 = N*sc instead of -N*sc); caught by curve-count mismatch (121 vs 656 curves) on the 7x25 q8 --rowY=2 sample before any solver run; fixed by deriving the sign from D<0 explicitly.
genfast2.js remains restricted to q >= w+1 like genfast.js (half-integer center census); for q <= w use sat2.js directly.
